# {Topic Name} · Product Architecture

**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Version:** v1
**Status:** Draft

**Decision-doc:** `{/<cycle_id>/lulu-bet/decision-doc.md}`

**Chain domain:** Topic product architecture shaping — structural product consensus for a multi-feature topic, reviewable before opening a feature cycle; not enterprise portfolio planning, not feature PRD (lulu-spec), not technical architecture (lulu-arch). Register rules and audience: see domain-instance.

---

SI.heading: Situation & Direction
SI.intent: Problem domain and convergence direction for product architecture exploration: (1) trigger — why product shaping happens now; (2) current product situation — verified user, market, and constraint state; (3) impact — cost of leaving product uncertainty unresolved; (4) direction — the topic-level product direction this exploration converges toward (observable, reviewable, not a feature backlog).
SI.intent_boundary: Scope boundaries, excluded product paths, capability partitioning, key decision detail, and open questions belong to BD, PS, PR, and OQ. Feature acceptance criteria, user-story detail, and technical architecture belong to downstream lulu-spec / lulu-arch / lulu-approach.

BD.heading: Boundaries
BD.intent: The boundary set for this product exploration as a whole: which user segments, capability domains, or product surfaces are in scope for shaping; product paths explicitly not chosen; product constraints and invariants that must hold across future features. Scope, exclusions, and constraints are presented together to protect the direction in SI from dilution.
BD.intent_boundary: Capability layout and user-value partitioning belong to PS. Trade-off comparison and adopt/reject rationale belong to PR. Blocking assumptions belong to OQ. Enterprise-wide portfolio restructuring and single-feature PRD detail are out of scope unless authorized in decision-doc.

PS.heading: Product Shape
PS.intent: Topic-level product structure view: core capabilities or value domains, responsibility partitioning, dependency direction among product surfaces; how future features attach to this structure (milestone granularity, not user-story backlog). When cross-domain user journeys matter at topic level, name the architecturally significant capability boundaries sufficient for downstream lulu-approach to inherit product premises without re-deriving partitions.
PS.intent_boundary: Feature-level user stories and acceptance criteria belong to lulu-spec. Technical module layout belongs to lulu-arch. Decision rationale belongs to PR.

PR.heading: Product Rationale
PR.intent: Adopted product judgments, rejected alternative directions and rationale (including explicitly rejected paths), reversibility, and evolution premises. Rationale is product-level trade-off reasoning, not authorization statements alone and not feature-level PRD detail.
PR.intent_boundary: Capability layout belongs to PS. Assumptions awaiting closure belong to OQ. Technical architecture and implementation tactics belong to downstream lulu-approach / lulu-arch.

OQ.heading: Open Questions
OQ.intent: Product assumptions, open questions, and risks not yet closed at topic level; each item labeled whether it blocks opening a new feature cycle (blocks-next-cycle or non-blocking) and anchored to the gap in SI, PS, or PR it closes.
OQ.intent_boundary: Closed decisions belong to PR. Feature acceptance criteria and technical verification gaps belong to downstream lulu-spec / lulu-arch.
